description: A narrow-scope, time-boxed engagement (6-10 weeks) designed to prove feasibility of a single AI use case before committing to a larger rollout.
target_conditions: Best for clients with low-to-medium data maturity who want to test AI value before large investment, on a single well-defined use case.
strengths: Low upfront cost; fast time-to-value; low client commitment risk; builds internal buy-in through visible quick wins.
weaknesses: Rarely scales into production without a larger follow-on engagement; revenue per project is small; can produce a stream of successful pilots that never mature into recurring revenue.
recommended_use_cases: Early-stage AI exploration; clients testing internal appetite for AI; low-budget proof-of-concept requests.

description: A large-scope, multi-year engagement covering strategy, data platform, model development, and organizational change across an entire client organization.
target_conditions: Requires strong executive sponsorship and significant budget; underperforms badly if sponsorship weakens mid-engagement.
strengths: High revenue potential; deep client relationship; strong ROI when executed with sustained sponsorship.
weaknesses: High complexity increases risk of delay and budget overrun, especially in heavily regulated industries; vulnerable to organizational resistance and sponsor turnover.
recommended_use_cases: Large enterprise clients with board-level AI mandates and multi-year budget commitments.

description: An approach that prioritizes building clean, centralized, governed data infrastructure before any AI or analytics use cases are built on top of it.
target_conditions: Assumes the client's existing data infrastructure and governance culture are reasonably mature; performs poorly when this assumption is wrong.
strengths: Produces durable, reusable data foundations; downstream AI projects built on top tend to perform better and faster.
weaknesses: Long time-to-first-value frustrates stakeholders expecting quick AI wins; if client data maturity is overestimated at proposal stage, the project frequently runs over budget and schedule before any AI value is delivered.
recommended_use_cases: Clients with fragmented legacy data systems planning multiple future AI initiatives, not just one.

description: An approach centered on customer experience use cases (personalization, recommendation, service automation), driven by customer research rather than technical feasibility alone.
target_conditions: Works well for B2C-heavy clients with accessible customer interaction data.
strengths: High customer/user satisfaction scores; strong internal champions from marketing/CX teams.
weaknesses: Financial ROI can lag satisfaction scores, especially when the business case wasn't tightly tied to a revenue or cost metric upfront.
recommended_use_cases: Retail, telecom, and insurance clients seeking to improve customer experience metrics.

description: An approach that targets high-volume, repetitive back-office processes for automation (RPA plus lightweight AI) before pursuing more advanced AI use cases.
target_conditions: Performs strongly in operationally repetitive environments; higher risk in environments with heavy regulatory or clinical judgment requirements.
strengths: Fast, measurable operational efficiency gains; relatively low technical risk; clear cost-savings business case.
weaknesses: Underdelivers on innovation narrative; in regulated environments, automating processes involving clinical or legal judgment can create compliance risk if oversight is inadequate.
recommended_use_cases: Manufacturing and logistics back-office and operations processes with high transaction volume.

description: An approach that begins with migrating client infrastructure to the cloud before layering AI and analytics capabilities on top.
target_conditions: Effective for clients still on legacy on-premise infrastructure; adds little value for clients already cloud-native.
strengths: Improves scalability and lowers long-term infrastructure cost; enables faster AI deployment cycles once complete.
weaknesses: Migration phase itself carries schedule risk independent of the AI use case; can be perceived by clients as an infrastructure project rather than an AI project, weakening executive visibility.
recommended_use_cases: Clients with legacy on-premise systems planning a broader technology modernization.

description: An approach that embeds governance, fairness testing, explainability, and compliance review throughout the AI development lifecycle.
target_conditions: Essential for regulated industries; adds overhead with limited perceived value for lower-risk, internal-only use cases.
strengths: Reduces regulatory and reputational risk; often required for client legal sign-off in regulated sectors; builds long-term trust.
weaknesses: Adds process overhead and can slow delivery timelines; in lower-risk projects, clients sometimes perceive it as unnecessary bureaucracy that inflates cost.
recommended_use_cases: Regulated-industry clients (banking, healthcare, government, insurance) and any project involving decisions affecting individuals.

description: An approach that treats the AI capability as an ongoing internal product with a dedicated roadmap, rather than a one-off delivered project.
target_conditions: Requires the client to have (or build) an internal product team to own the capability after handover; underperforms when no such ownership exists.
strengths: Higher long-term adoption; capability continues to improve after the consulting engagement ends.
weaknesses: If the client lacks a receiving product team, the capability often stagnates or is abandoned shortly after project close, despite strong metrics during the engagement itself.
recommended_use_cases: Clients with existing digital product organizations who can absorb ownership after delivery.

description: A phased approach that modernizes legacy systems and processes in small, low-risk increments rather than a single large transformation.
target_conditions: Works well for risk-averse clients or those with mission-critical legacy systems that cannot tolerate downtime.
strengths: Lower risk of catastrophic failure; easier to secure ongoing budget approval phase by phase.
weaknesses: Slower overall time-to-full-value; risk of losing momentum or executive attention between phases, especially if account ownership changes.
recommended_use_cases: Risk-averse clients with mission-critical legacy systems, particularly banking core systems and government infrastructure.

description: An iterative approach: build a minimum viable capability, measure real usage data, and iterate based on findings.
target_conditions: Requires a client culture comfortable with iteration and imperfect early versions; struggles with clients expecting a fully specified deliverable upfront.
strengths: Adapts quickly to real usage patterns; avoids over-investing in features nobody uses.
weaknesses: Clients expecting traditional fixed-scope delivery can perceive this approach as ambiguous or under-planned, creating friction during contracting and steering committee reviews.
recommended_use_cases: Clients open to agile, iterative engagement models, typically in product or digital-native business units.

description: An approach that builds a single shared AI/ML platform and center of excellence serving multiple business units within the client organization.
target_conditions: Requires strong central IT/data governance authority; underperforms in organizations where business units operate with high autonomy.
strengths: Economies of scale; consistent governance; easier to maintain and monitor across use cases.
weaknesses: Business units with strong autonomy often resist adoption of a centrally-imposed platform, leading to shadow-IT workarounds and lower actual usage than platform metrics suggest.
recommended_use_cases: Clients with centralized IT governance and multiple business units needing similar AI capabilities.

description: An approach where individual business units fund and own their own AI initiatives with light central coordination, rather than a single central platform.
target_conditions: Works well in decentralized organizations; leads to duplicated effort and inconsistent quality in more centralized organizations.
strengths: Faster buy-in from business units directly funding the work; solutions closely tailored to specific unit needs.
weaknesses: Can produce redundant, inconsistent, or contradictory AI capabilities across units when the client organization actually has stronger central governance than assumed at proposal stage.
recommended_use_cases: Decentralized client organizations where business units control their own technology budgets.
